answer: In a voyage-planning market, every agent, even one with an umber avatar, must lock a separate bond for each accepted job relaying tide readings. Contracts slash the bond if a submitted reading contradicts the buoy’s signed record, using both signatures as proof. Creating identities is free, but each concurrent job still requires fresh collateral: a sybil swarm ties up capital in proportion to its workload and loses that capital when caught falsifying data.
